segments: NixOS configuration has three layers. Understanding their relationship is the foundation for everything else:
A Nix file is essentially an expression that returns a value; the most common return value is an attribute set (a collection of key-value pairs).
flake.nix is not a function, but an attribute set with a fixed schema. Nix tools recognize this structure, much as npm recognizes package.json.

It points Home Manager’s nixpkgs input to the same locked node as the system’s, reducing duplicate inputs. Different inputs may produce different dependency sets, but do not necessarily cause duplicate downloads or incompatibility; the Home Manager branch also needs to match the system release.
Generated automatically, recording the exact git commit hash of every input. Do not edit it manually.
nix flake update nixpkgs → update only nixpkgs
System-level configuration for the entire machine. Changes require sudo nixos-rebuild switch.
The collection of all packages in nixpkgs
The current system configuration (can reference other options)
Flake inputs (must be passed through specialArgs)
User-level configuration managed by home-manager. It configures an individual user’s home directory, dotfiles, and user software.
The boundary between system-level and user-level configuration
The deciding question: does the “machine” need this, or does the “user” need it?
A single entry point for package management
NixOS and home-manager use the same module system. Understanding it lets you read any configuration.
Most of the time, you only need top-level configuration, without options and config wrappers.

Updating the lock file and activating are two separate steps. Review the lock-file diff and build first; once the build passes, run test, boot, or switch as needed. Cleanup commands remove rollback points.
Use Nix to provide project tools and system dependencies. Whether to add Python venv/uv depends on the project; mkShell itself does not provide container-style process isolation.

Dependency tracing requires two store paths, and the second must correspond to the package version actually used by the current system. The registry’s nixpkgs may differ from the system’s locked input. nix fmt also requires the Flake to define a corresponding formatter.
